SUPERVISOR DISPATCH — the data store moves to a real database. Marker: STOREDB-0606, ledger req_0048.

USER RULING (with the live failure on their screen), verbatim: "its data store across the board. i am finding [store unavailable: data store: corrupt record at cart/hmsc-int/data/streams/sessions.jsonl:884] we need to move to pg or sqlite which are in the framework already."

TWO STEPS, STRICT ORDER — the user's store is DOWN right now:

STEP 0 — TRIAGE (commit today, first): the reader must honor the V20 tolerance law that already exists on paper ("boundary validation never throws"): a corrupt/partial record in any stream file is SKIPPED + logged loudly + quarantined in memory — the fold continues with every valid record. The file is NEVER rewritten (append-only is sacred; no "repair" writes). The user's store comes back with all 883 good records the moment this lands. THEN the forensics, read-only: what is physically at sessions.jsonl:884 — a torn/interleaved append? Two writers? Report the mechanism with the bytes. Prime suspect: MULTIPLE app instances (user session + census walks + headless verify boots) appending the same file with no locking — name it if the bytes say so.

STEP 1 — THE MIGRATION: stream backing moves to a database already in the framework (has-pg exists; check for sqlite support — pick per fit and SAY WHY; sqlite/WAL is the likely local-first answer, pg if the framework's sqlite story is weaker than I think). NON-NEGOTIABLE: V20 SEMANTICS SURVIVE EXACTLY — append-only event log, per-concern streams, the one global sequence, undo points as log positions, snapshots for compile/, schema evolution by addition, total history that cannot break. Only the BACKING changes (jsonl files -> DB tables). The swap happens BEHIND the existing store door (editors/store.ts + sessions.ts and the *.test.ts contracts) — consumers must not change; the door is deep (P3), the suites that pin stream behavior keep passing untouched where the contract allows.
- Concurrency is the point: single-writer/WAL transaction semantics so N app instances can never tear a record again. Prove it: a P4 test with two writers hammering one stream — zero corruption, total order preserved.
- INGEST: one-time import of every existing .jsonl (all streams, all workspaces) into the DB — byte-faithful per record, the :884 corrupt record quarantined + logged, originals left in place untouched as the archive (never deleted by you; the user retires them).
- Storage location stays gitignored per V20; snapshot system updated same-commit if the snapshot reader changes (V20: "a new stream without snapshot support is an incomplete change" applies to the backing too).
- Docs: V20's storage section + STRUCTURE + _index records updated same-commit; this is backing-implementation, not a law change — note that explicitly in DECISIONS only if oracle review says the V20 text mentions jsonl specifically.

Process: explicit paths; tutorial-grade commits (step 0 alone first); NO desktop capture; if a framework gap blocks (sqlite binding missing a needed surface), STOP and report; resolve req_0048 step-wise. READY FOR USER TEST after step 0 (their store works again) and again after step 1 (same store, real backing, two-writer-proof).
